_comment: The road vehicles of a German module. Edit this, not mods/cars/ — everything
under there is generated by build_cars.mjs.
The meshes are generated models (Tripo) that were exported as FBX: one nameless
mesh apiece, one baked texture atlas, about eleven thousand triangles, and
everything the generator thought it saw — a plinth under the car, an interior
behind the windows, the inside of its own shell. The build finds all three by
looking at the geometry and throws them away (`lib/clean.mjs`), because there
are no object names to go by.
`length_m`, `width_m` and `height_m` are the real dimensions of the vehicle.
The models arrive normalised into a unit box, so these are what gives them a
size at all — and they are not decoration: the imagery detection checks a find
against the size of the class it claims to be, and a car park is laid out on
the assumption that a bay is 2.5 m wide.
`nose` says which way the model faces before the build turns it; the game's
convention is the front along −Z (MODS.md, Track objects).
`width_m` is the body, `mirrors_m` the width over the wing mirrors — and the
second is the one the build checks against, because a bounding box has the
mirrors in it. Both are stated because the first is what a bay is measured for
and the second is what the model actually spans.
`waist` is where the glasshouse starts, as a share of the vehicle's height. A
van's waistline sits much lower down its body than a saloon's, which is why it
The build measures what came out against `width_m`/`mirrors_m`/`height_m` and
warns past five per cent. Those two are not inputs — the scale comes from the
length alone — they are the prediction that says whether the model and the
entry describe the same vehicle.

source.note: Generated with a 3D tool and exported as FBX; the zips are unpacked into cache/cars/manual/src-<id>/ by import_cars.mjs.

_levels: What each level keeps of the cleaned mesh, and how far it reaches [m].
The reaches are short because a car is small: at ninety metres it is fifty
pixels long, at two hundred and fifty it is eighteen. `--preview` draws the
hand-over sheets that say whether a step is visible; they are the only
honest way to pick these numbers.

types._length_note: 4.05 m is what a Kleinwagen of this kind measures; this model's own proportions fit the class figures best at this length, so this is what it is built to. The build warns when the two disagree by more than a twentieth.

4.24 m is what a Kompakt-SUV of this kind measures; this model's own proportions fit the class figures best at this length, so this is what it is built to. The build warns when the two disagree by more than a twentieth.

4.9 m is what a Transporter of this kind measures; this model's own proportions fit the class figures best at this length, so this is what it is built to. The build warns when the two disagree by more than a twentieth.
types._tolerance: This model comes out about a tenth lower than a real T6.1 — 1.82 m against 1.99 — and wide with it. Nothing in the pipeline caused that and no uniform scale can fix it; the vehicle is simply proportioned like a lowered van. Looked at and accepted, which is what this figure records.
